    title: "Privacy Policy"

    ## Scope, Effective Date, and Covered Entities           
                                                             
    * **Effective Date:** November 10, 2026                  
    * **Entities Covered:** `alanpruitt.com` (Educational    
    Manifesto & Essay Publishing), `webcognita.com`          
    (Webcognita LLC Consulting & Digital Assets), and        
    companion client-side educational utilities (including   
    `exwtoolkit.com`).                                       
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 1. Overview and Commitment to Privacy                
                                                             
    Webcognita LLC (a Veteran-Owned Small Business) and Alan 
    Pruitt ("we," "our," or "us") respect your digital       
    privacy. This Privacy Policy outlines the minimal data   
    collection practices associated with our web properties. 
    We operate under strict data minimalism, transparency,   
    and the principles of Curriculum-as-Code. We do not sell,
    rent, trade, or monetize visitor data, nor do we use     
    visitor communications or client records to train public 
    foundational AI models.                                  
                                                             
    * **Institutional Separation Notice:** `alanpruitt.com`  
    and `webcognita.com` are operated independently by Alan  
    Pruitt and Webcognita LLC. These platforms do not        
    collect, process, or store student educational records   
    (FERPA) or protected health information (HIPAA) on behalf
    of Arizona Western College or any partner institution.   
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 2. Information We Collect                            
                                                             
    We collect only the essential data required to deliver   
    static content and fulfill professional consulting or    
    educational transactions:                                
                                                             
    * **Passive Technical Telemetry:** When you visit        
    `alanpruitt.com` or `webcognita.com`, standard server    
    logs processed via our static hosting and edge delivery  
    infrastructure (including GitHub Pages and Cloudflare    
    DNS/TLS routing) may automatically record basic          
    connection data, such as your IP address, browser type,  
    operating system, and access timestamps. This data is    
    used solely for network security, routing, and uptime    
    maintenance.                                             
    * **Active User Submissions:** If you contact us directly
    via email or purchase professional services or digital   
    products via Webcognita LLC, we collect the necessary    
    contact details (such as your name, institutional        
    affiliation, and email address) solely to respond to your
    inquiries or fulfill your order.                         
    * **Zero-PII Client-Side Simulators:** Interactive       
    calculators and educational simulators (such as the ADA  
    Title II ROI Calculator on `alanpruitt.com` and clinical 
    teaching tools on `exwtoolkit.com`) execute entirely     
    within your local browser memory. No user inputs,        
    simulated vitals, or institutional financial models are

    or "Institution") entering into a Master Services        
    Agreement, Statement of Work (SOW), Purchase Order, or   
    digital product licensing agreement with Webcognita LLC. 
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 1. Purpose, Scope, and Order of Precedence           
                                                             
    This Data Processing Addendum ("DPA") supplements the    
    Webcognita LLC Terms of Service and any governing        
    institutional contract, Purchase Order, or Statement of  
    Work (SOW). This DPA ensures strict compliance with      
    statutory data privacy, accessibility, and AI governance 
    mandates, including the **Family Educational Rights and  
    Privacy Act (FERPA, 20 U.S.C. § 1232g; 34 CFR Part 99)**,
    **DOJ ADA Title II (28 CFR Part 35)**, state-level       
    student and public data privacy statutes, and            
    institutional IT security policies. In the event of any  
    conflict between the terms of this DPA and the general   
    Terms of Service, the terms of this DPA shall govern.    
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 2. FERPA Compliance & Educational Records            
                                                             
    1. **Default Zero-PII Architecture by Design:**          
    Webcognita LLC engineers its Curriculum-as-Code          
    frameworks, static web infrastructure, and client-side   
    browser simulators (`exwtoolkit.com`) to operate without 
    collecting, transmitting, or storing student personally  
    identifiable information (PII). Unless explicitly        
    required by a written Statement of Work, the Institution 
    does not need to provision student PII to Webcognita LLC.
    2. **School Official Designation (`34 CFR §              
    99.31(a)(1)(i)(B)`):** To the extent that Webcognita LLC 
    receives, accesses, or maintains education records (as   
    defined under FERPA, `34 CFR Part 99`) on behalf of the  
    Institution under a specific Statement of Work, Provider 
    acknowledges that it acts as a "School Official" with a  
    legitimate educational interest and operates under the   
    direct control of the Institution with respect to the    
    use, maintenance, and handling of such education records.
    3. **Prohibition on Unauthorized Disclosure &            
    Re-Disclosure (`34 CFR § 99.33`):** Webcognita LLC shall 
    not use, disclose, or re-disclose any education records  
    or personally identifiable information (PII) derived from
    student records for any purpose other than fulfilling the
    specific contractual deliverables outlined in the        
    governing Statement of Work.                             
    4. **Strict Data Minimization:** Provider shall collect  
    and process only the absolute minimum institutional or   
    faculty data necessary to execute consulting, training,  
    accessibility auditing, or software integration services.
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 3. AI Data Governance, Air-Gapped Sovereignty, and   
    Zero-Retention Mandates                                  
                                                             
    1. **Strict Prohibition on Foundation Model Training:**  
    Webcognita LLC explicitly certifies that **no Customer   
    data, user inputs, uploaded documents, prompts, source   
    code, or institutional content processed via Webcognita  
    LLC systems or associated AI workflows shall ever be used
    to train, fine-tune, or improve public or third-party    
    foundational machine learning models**.                  
    2. **Air-Gapped Local Inference & Zero-Retention         
    Enterprise APIs:** Any artificial intelligence models or 
    automated auditing tools deployed by Webcognita LLC in   
    connection with institutional contracts operate          
    exclusively via either: (a) **air-gapped local hardware  
    inference (`Zero Cloud Egress`)** where all computation  
    remains on local encrypted workstations, or (b)          
    **enterprise-grade, zero-retention API endpoints** where 
    input and output payloads are processed ephemerally and  
    purged immediately following query resolution.           
    3. **Federal AI Literacy & Risk Alignment:** All AI      
    governance workflows and instructional deliverables align
    with the **NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF     
    1.0)** and the **U.S. Department of Labor (DOL)          
    Employment and Training Administration (ETA) Training and
    Employment Notice (TEN) No. 07-25 (*Artificial           
    Intelligence Literacy Framework*)**.                     
    4. **No Third-Party Monetization:** Institutional data   
    and intellectual property assets shall never be          
    monetized, aggregated for commercial profiling, or shared
    with unauthorized third-party entities.                  
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 4. Sub-Processor Inventory & Supply Chain            
    Transparency                                             
                                                             
    Webcognita LLC maintains a minimal, transparent inventory
    of authorized infrastructure providers utilized in       
    delivering static web assets, documentation, and billing:
                                                             
    * **Static Hosting & Version Control:** GitHub Pages /   
    GitHub Enterprise (Static asset hosting,                 
    version-controlled repositories, and automated CI/CD     
    deployment).                                             
    * **Edge DNS & TLS Security Routing:** Cloudflare, Inc.  
    (DNS resolution, DDoS mitigation, and enforced TLS/HTTPS 
    transport encryption).                                   
    * **Payment Processing (If Applicable):** Stripe, Inc.   
    (Tokenized PCI-DSS Level 1 compliant financial           
    transaction handling; payment card credentials never     
    touch Webcognita LLC servers).                           
    * **Sub-Processor Obligations:** Webcognita LLC binds all
    authorized sub-processors to data protection and security
    standards no less restrictive than those outlined in this
    DPA. The Institution will be provided written notice     
    prior to the addition of any new sub-processor that      
    processes institutional data.                            
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 5. Data Security, Accessibility Compliance, and      
    Breach Notification                                      
                                                             
    1. **Technical & Administrative Safeguards:** Webcognita 
    LLC implements industry-standard administrative,         
    physical, and technical safeguards, including enforced   
    TLS 1.3 / HTTPS encryption for data in transit, AES-256  
    encryption for data at rest, hardware-backed multi-factor
    authentication (MFA) for administrative access, and      
    static architecture designs that eliminate server-side   
    database injection surfaces.                             
    2. **Digital Accessibility Standards (`ADA Title II` •   
    `WCAG 2.2 AA` • `Section 508`):** All digital assets,    
    consulting courseware, and web applications delivered by 
    Webcognita LLC are engineered and continuously audited to
    comply with **WCAG 2.2 Level AA** (including             
    high-contrast `9:1` visual readability gates), **DOJ ADA 
    Title II (`28 CFR Part 35`)**, and **Section 508 of the  
    Rehabilitation Act (`36 CFR Part 1194`)**.               
    3. **48-Hour Security Incident Notification:** In the    
    event of a confirmed or reasonably suspected security    
    breach compromising institutional data or education      
    records, Webcognita LLC shall notify the Institution's   
    designated procurement officer and legal counsel without 
    unreasonable delay—and in no event later than            
    **forty-eight (48) hours** following discovery—providing 
    full cooperation and forensic telemetry to mitigate the  
    incident.                                                
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 6. Data Return and Certified Permanent Deletion      
                                                             
    Upon the expiration, termination, or completion of the   
    governing Statement of Work or contract:                 
                                                             
    1. **Secure Purging (30-Day Window):** Webcognita LLC    
    shall, within **thirty (30) calendar days** (or sooner if
    requested in writing by the Institution), securely       
    return, delete, purge, and destroy all institutional     
    data, confidential communication records, and            
    education-related files from its active systems and      
    non-archival backups.                                    
    2. **Certificate of Destruction:** Upon written request  
    by the Institution, an authorized principal of Webcognita
    LLC shall provide formal written certification confirming
    that all institutional data has been permanently and     
    securely destroyed.                                      
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 7. Governing Law and Institutional Jurisdiction      
                                                             
    This DPA shall be governed by and construed in accordance
    with the federal laws of the United States and the state 
    laws of the jurisdiction governing the contracting       
    educational institution or public agency (or the State of
    Arizona if not otherwise specified by statute), without  
    regard to conflict of law principles.

    ## Institutional IP Ownership, Work-for-Hire & OER       
    Licensing Rider                                          
                                                             
    * **Effective Date:** November 10, 2026                  
    * **Entity:** Webcognita LLC (a Veteran-Owned Small      
    Business) and Alan Pruitt ("Provider," "we," or "our")   
    * **Applicable To:** All educational institutions,       
    community colleges, universities, public workforce       
    agencies, and government contracting bodies ("Customer"  
    or "Institution") entering into a Master Services        
    Agreement, Statement of Work (SOW), Purchase Order, or   
    grant sub-award with Webcognita LLC.                     
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 1. Pre-Existing Provider Intellectual Property       
    ("Background IP")                                        
                                                             
    1. **Definition of Provider IP:** "Provider IP" means all
    proprietary software codebases, compilers, architectural 
    frameworks, templates, pre-existing digital assets,      
    courseware structures, documentation, know-how, and      
    methodologies developed, acquired, or authored by        
    Webcognita LLC or Alan Pruitt prior to or independently  
    of the governing Statement of Work (SOW). Provider IP    
    explicitly includes, without limitation:                 
       * **Curriculum-as-Code (C-a-C)** publishing, linting, 
       and Zero-Drift synchronization pipelines;             
       * **The Clinical Framing Protocol (`Pattern / Rule /  
       Solve`)** and **Mission Loop** pedagogical            
       architectures;                                        
       * **The 10-7-0 Mastery Grading Scale** and **Active   
       Verification** assessment telemetry frameworks;       
       * **POUR, WCAG 2.2 AA, and WCAG 3.0 Atomic            
       Accessibility Linters** and **9:1 High-Contrast**     
       remediation engines; and                              
       * **Client-side edge simulator engines                
       (`exwtoolkit.com`)** and **local air-gapped AI        
       auditing workflows (`Argon 4` / `Gemma 4`)**.         
    2. **Reservation of Rights:** Provider retains sole and  
    exclusive ownership of all right, title, and interest in 
    and to Provider IP, including all applicable copyright,  
    trademark, patent, and trade secret rights. Nothing in   
    any governing contract, Purchase Order, or SOW shall be  
    construed to transfer or assign ownership of Provider IP 
    to the Customer.                                         
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 2. Institutional Client Intellectual Property and    
    Custom Deliverables                                      
                                                             
    1. **Client IP Ownership:** Customer retains sole and    
    exclusive ownership of all pre-existing institutional    
    materials, logos, trademarks, syllabus templates, and    
    proprietary institutional data supplied to Provider for  
    the purpose of executing the consulting engagement or    
    digital product build ("Customer IP").                   
    2. **Custom Deliverables & Work-for-Hire:** Unless       
    otherwise specified in an explicit, signed Statement of  
    Work, custom courseware, specific curriculum             
    documentation, or bespoke digital assets explicitly      
    commissioned and paid for by the Customer under a        
    designated commercial fee structure shall be licensed or 
    assigned to the Customer as agreed upon in writing. In   
    the absence of an express written assignment, upon full  
    payment of all applicable fees, Customer is granted a    
    perpetual, non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free 
    license to use, adapt, and distribute such custom        
    deliverables solely for the Customer's internal          
    educational and administrative operations.               
    3. **Embedded Provider IP:** To the extent that any      
    custom deliverable incorporates or relies upon embedded  
    components of Pre-Existing Provider IP (such as          
    accessible HTML/CSS component templates, rubric          
    structures, or client-side calculator embeds), Provider  
    retains full ownership of such Provider IP and grants the
    Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license
    to use those embedded components solely as integrated    
    within the delivered courseware. Customer may not        
    extract, resell, or sublicense embedded Provider IP as a 
    standalone commercial product or service.                
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 3. Open Educational Resources (OER) and Creative     
    Commons Licensing                                        
                                                             
    1. **OER Designation:** Where a Statement of Work, grant 
    agreement, or public repository explicitly designates    
    specific curriculum deliverables, toolkits, or           
    educational modules as Open Educational Resources (OER), 
    such materials shall be licensed under either the        
    **Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License 
    (`CC BY 4.0`)** or the **Creative Commons                
    Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International   
    License (`CC BY-NC-SA 4.0`)**, as explicitly marked on   
    the deliverable or agreed upon in the governing Statement
    of Work.                                                 
    2. **Attribution Requirements:** When distributing,      
    remixing, or adapting OER deliverables authored by       
    Webcognita LLC or Alan Pruitt, Customer and all          
    downstream users must preserve all copyright and         
    provenance notices and provide clear attribution to      
    **Alan Pruitt (`alanpruitt.com`) and Webcognita LLC** as 
    the original creators.                                   
    3. **Strict Exclusion of Proprietary Code & Orchestration
    Engines:** Open Educational Resources licenses apply     
    strictly to designated curriculum text, instructional    
    tables, and static educational media. **Under no         
    circumstances shall an OER license be interpreted to     
    grant open-source ownership, source-code redistribution  
    rights, or commercial licensing to the underlying        
    proprietary software architectures, CI/CD compilers,     
    automated grading engines, AI orchestration frameworks,  
    or proprietary codebases owned by Webcognita LLC.**      
    4. **Federal Grant & Public Agency Open-Licensing        
    Alignment (`2 CFR § 200.315` • `29 CFR § 2900.13`):** For
    engagements funded in whole or in part by federal grants 
    (including U.S. Department of Labor ETA and National     
    Science Foundation awards), newly commissioned curriculum
    text funded directly by the award shall satisfy          
    applicable federal open-licensing mandates, while all    
    pre-existing **Provider IP** and independently developed 
    software tools remain the exclusive property of          
    Webcognita LLC pursuant to federal pre-existing          
    intellectual property protections.                       
                                                             
    ---                                                      
                                                             
    ### 4. Warranty of Originality and Institutional         
    Separation                                               
                                                             
    1. **Warranty of Originality:** Provider warrants and    
    represents that all deliverables provided under a        
    governing Statement of Work are original works authored  
    by Provider or that Provider has secured all necessary   
    licenses, rights, and permissions to deliver such works  
    without infringing the copyright, trademark, patent,     
    trade secret, or privacy rights of any third party.      
    2. **Institutional Separation Notice:** Webcognita LLC (a
    Veteran-Owned Small Business) and Alan Pruitt operate    
    independently of Arizona Western College and any other   
    academic employer. All Provider IP and commercial        
    consulting deliverables are developed independently on   
    private hardware and infrastructure without the use of   
    public institutional funds or facilities.

    ### 5. Order of Precedence and Contact Information

  ### 1. The Single-Member LLC (SOLE MBR) Line 1 / Line 2 /  
  Line 3a Rule                                               
                                                             
  • Pattern: Your                                            
  Webcognita LLC IRS Letter 147C 81-0809739.pdf establishes  
  the entity as:                                             
      • WEBCOGNITA LLC / ALAN LEE PRUITT SOLE MBR (EIN: 81-  
      0809739, 1906 S 6TH AVE, YUMA, AZ 85364-5513).         
  • Rule (IRS Form W-9 Rev. March 2024 Instructions):        
  Unless Webcognita LLC has filed Form 2553/8832 to be taxed 
  as an S-Corp or C-Corp, the IRS classifies a Single-Member 
  LLC as a Disregarded Entity, which requires:               
      • Line 1 (Name of entity/individual): Alan Lee Pruitt  
      • Line 2 (Business name/disregarded entity name):      
      Webcognita LLC                                         
      • Line 3a (Federal tax classification): Check          
      Individual/sole proprietor (the first checkbox—per IRS 
      instructions, you do NOT check the "Limited liability  
      company" box for a single-member disregarded LLC).     
      • Line 5 & Line 6 (Address): 1906 S 6th Ave • Yuma, AZ 
      85364-5513                                             
      • Line 7 (List account number(s) here — optional):     
      SAM.gov UEI: EZ34U9KNJA17 | CAGE: 4ZCN6 | NAICS: 611430,
      611710, 541511                                         
      (Pre-populating Line 7 with your SAM.gov UEI & CAGE    
      links the W-9 directly to your federal vendor profile  
      for institutional auditors.)                           
      • Part I (Taxpayer Identification Number — TIN): Enter 
      81 - 0809739 in the Employer identification number     
      (EIN) boxes, and explicitly leave the Social Security  
      Number (SSN) boxes blank (N/A / masked). Never expose  
      an SSN on any public or institutional W-9.

  ### 2. The Wet-Signature Fraud Risk on Public URLs (Part II
  Certification)                                             
                                                             
  • Pattern: If you host a clean, un-watermarked Form W-9    
  bearing your live signature (Alan_Pruitt_eSign.jpg) on a   
  public URL (webcognita.com/docs/), automated scrapers have 
  your Legal Name + LLC Name + Address + EIN: 81-0809739 +   
  IRS Letter 147C + Wet Signature—everything needed to spoof 
  vendor ACH change requests or file fraudulent 1099s.       
  • Rule: Publicly hosted verification documents should allow
  procurement officers to verify your exact W-9 tax          
  classification, address, and EIN immediately, while keeping
  your live wet signature restricted to direct PO / vendor-  
  portal onboarding.

  ### Argon 4 Evaluation & Recommendations for <footer>      
  (Pattern / Rule / Solve)                                   
                                                             
  Your proposed <footer> snippet is clean, compact, and      
  introduces two high-value additions that are not yet in    
  footer.html:                                               
                                                             
  1. A global Institutional Disclaimer (<p                   
  class="disclaimer">) in the site-wide footer (so every     
  page—not just individual essays—carries the institutional  
  separation firewall).                                      
  2. A direct /sitemap.xml link in the footer alongside the  
  legal links (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 "unless otherwise noted",     
  which also harmonizes with CC BY 4.0 on designated OER     
  packages).                                                 
                                                             
  Evaluated against WCAG 2.2 AA, W3C ARIA in HTML, our       
  Playwright CI audit (audit.js), and bilingual Hugo routing 
  (EN / ES), here are 5 concrete recommendations:            
  ──────                                                     
  ### 1. Remove Redundant role="contentinfo" & Use aria-label
  Instead                                                    
                                                             
  • Pattern: <footer class="site-footer" role="contentinfo"> 
  • Rule: Under the W3C ARIA in HTML specification, a top-   
  level <footer> already has the implicit landmark role      
  contentinfo. Automated accessibility linters (axe-core /   
  Lighthouse) flag explicit role="contentinfo" on <footer> as
  redundant.                                                 
  • Solve: Omit role="contentinfo" and use aria-label="Site  
  Footer" (Pie de página del sitio in Spanish).              
                                                             
  ### 2. Name the Specific Institutions in the Global <p     
  class="disclaimer">                                        
                                                             
  • Pattern: <p class="disclaimer">Disclaimer: Independent   
  faculty research and OER publishing. Views do not represent
  institutional policy.</p>                                  
  • Rule: Explicitly naming Webcognita LLC (VOSB), Arizona   
  Western College, and The University of Arizona in the      
  global footer disclaimer provides maximum legal clarity on 
  every page of the site.                                    
  • Solve:                                                   
  │ Disclaimer: Independent faculty research, software       
  │ engineering, and OER publishing by Alan Pruitt and       
  │ Webcognita LLC (VOSB). Views and architectures do not    
  │ represent official policy or endorsement by Arizona      
  │ Western College or The University of Arizona.            
                                                             
                                                             
  ### 3. Keep "Unless Otherwise Noted" on the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
  Line (Harmonizes with CC BY 4.0 OER Packages)              
                                                             
  • Pattern: "Published under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 unless         
  otherwise noted."                                          
  • Rule: Adding "unless otherwise noted" (or referencing    
  your IP & OER Licensing Rider /ip-oer/) is a smart legal   
  upgrade over the current footer.html:31 wording because    
  your syndicated OER .zip datasets use CC BY 4.0 while your 
  proprietary Webcognita LLC software engines are reserved   
  under /ip-oer/.

  Here is the Argon 4 Evaluation & Recommendation (Pattern / 
  Rule / Solve) for the Hugo <head> partial integration      
  instruction across your two repositories:                  
  ──────                                                     
  ### 1. Pattern (Context & Repository Architecture Audit)   
                                                             
  The integration guidance assumes a textbook Hugo setup     
  where both repositories have a single                      
  layouts/_default/baseof.html template with one <head>      
  block.                                                     
                                                             
  Auditing the actual template trees in alanpruitt.github.io 
  (Hugo v0.165.0) and webcognita (Static HTML5) revealed two 
  important architectural nuances:                           
                                                             
  1. Personal Repository (alanpruitt.github.io — 7           
  Independent <head> Templates, No baseof.html):             
  Instead of a single baseof.html, alanpruitt.github.io      
  defines independent <head> blocks across 7 layout files:   
      • index.html:44 (Already includes the master @graph    
      with @id: "https://alanpruitt.com/#person")            
      • single.html:54 (Already includes {{ partial "schema- 
      alanpruitt.html" . }})                                 
      • single.html:3 (Emits ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD        
      referencing @id: "https://alanpruitt.com/#person", but 
      does not yet include {{ partial "schema-alanpruitt.    
      html" . }})                                            
      • list.html:3 (Missing {{ partial "schema-alanpruitt.  
      html" . }} in <head>)                                  
      • list.html:3 (Missing {{ partial "schema-alanpruitt.  
      html" . }} in <head>)                                  
      • single.html:3 (Missing {{ partial "schema-alanpruitt.
      html" . }} in <head>)                                  
      • workshop-single.html:3 (Missing {{ partial "schema-  
      alanpruitt.html" . }} in <head>)                       
  2. LLC Repository (webcognita — Static HTML5 on GitHub     
  Pages):                                                    
      • webcognita.com                                       
      (/Users/alanpruitt/projects/webcognita) is deployed as 
      static HTML5 (not built by Hugo), and we already       
      injected the validated ProfessionalService JSON-LD     
      directly into <head> across all 10 .html pages         
      (80a81c3).                                             
      • However, storing the canonical partials directly     
      inside the LLC repository at                           
      /Users/alanpruitt/projects/webcognita/layouts/partials/
      schema-webcognita.html and                             
      /Users/alanpruitt/projects/webcognita/layouts/partials/
      footer-webcognita.html establishes a clean Single      
      Source of Truth (SSoT) inside webcognita itself.       
                                                             
  ──────                                                     
  ### 2. Rule (Constraint)                                   
                                                             
  1. 100% <head> Coverage on alanpruitt.com: Wire {{ partial 
  "schema-alanpruitt.html" . }} into the <head> of the 5

  "https://alanpruitt.com/#person" locally in <head>.

  layouts/partials/schema-alanpruitt.html + footer-          
  alanpruitt.html in alanpruitt.github.io, and place         
  layouts/partials/schema-webcognita.html + footer-          
  webcognita.html directly inside                            
  /Users/alanpruitt/projects/webcognita/layouts/partials/.

  • Actual WSGI Port: The multi-worker Gunicorn + Flask RAG

  of the time on M2.

  vs. exw-argon4-cac:latest)                                 
                                                             
  • Live Finding:

      agy (AGY_MODEL="gemini-4-carbon" in .zshrc:50), not a

  ### Carbon 4 Evaluation of { "defaultModel": "gemini-4-

  Evaluating that JSON snippet against the agy v1.5.5 CLI    
  schema and live agy models registry surfaced two schema    
  corrections and one system security boundary:              
                                                             
  1. Key Name ("model", not "defaultModel"):                 
      • In ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json, the      
      official key is "model". An unrecognized "defaultModel"
      key is silently ignored by agy.                        
  2. Exact Model Slug (gemini-4-carbon-medium / -high / -    
  low):                                                      
      • Running agy models shows agy v1.5.5 requires the     
      effort suffix rather than bare "gemini-4-carbon":      
          • "gemini-4-carbon-medium" — Gemini 4 Carbon       
          (Medium)                                           
          • "gemini-4-carbon-high" — Gemini 4 Carbon (High)  
          • "gemini-4-carbon-low" — Gemini 4 Carbon (Low)    
      • Valid settings.json entry:                           
        {                                                    
          "model": "gemini-4-carbon-medium"                  
        }                                                    
                                                             
  3. Hardcoded System Protection Boundary on settings.json:  
      • ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json is gated by  
      Antigravity's hardcoded system protection rule         
      (Permission denied... Matches hardcoded system         
      protection boundary rule), so agents are blocked from  
      editing settings.json directly.

  ### 2. High-Value CI Blind Spot Caught During Inspection   
  (fetch-depth: 1)                                           
                                                             
  Inspecting the live logs of Run 42935311766 revealed a     
  subtle shallow-clone blind spot in carbon4-audit.yml and   
  qm-audit.yml:                                              
                                                             
  • Both workflows call uses: actions/checkout@v4 without    
  fetch-depth: 0, so GitHub Actions defaults to fetch-depth: 
  1 (fetching only HEAD, without HEAD~1).                    
  • Because carbon4_linter.py:41-48 detects pushed files in  
  CI via git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACM HEAD~1 HEAD, 
  HEAD~1 fails on a depth-1 checkout—causing carbon4_linter. 
  py to silently print [PASS] Carbon 4 Linter: No staged     
  curriculum files to audit on every push.                   
  • Additionally, once fetch-depth: 0 is enabled so          
  carbon4_linter.py audits pushed .md/.html files, its sub-  
  gates (canvas_accessibility_rules.py and                   
  argon4_wcag3_plain_language_engine.py) require pip install 
  beautifulsoup4 requests markdown python-dotenv in those two
  workflows.                                                 
  ──────                                                     
  ### 3. Recommendations                                     
                                                             
  1. Fix fetch-depth: 0 + Dependencies + Python 3.11 in      
  carbon4-audit.yml and qm-audit.yml: Ensure carbon4_linter. 
  py can always diff HEAD~1..HEAD and import bs4 + requests  
  when curriculum files change.                              
  2. Add python3 scripts/carbon4_linter.py to                
  exw_pipeline.yml:45-49: Run all three linters              
  (pii_security_linter.py,                                   
  exw_accessibility_pre_commit_linter.py, and carbon4_linter.
  py) together in the main pipeline job as well.

  ### 2. One-Click Sweep for Your Cloud Google Drive Project 
  Horizon Folder                                             
                                                             
  Because Google Drive is not mounted locally on M2          
  (~/Library/CloudStorage has no Drive mount and no OAuth    
  token is stored on disk), the safest way to update every   
  cloud Google Doc in-place—preserving 100% of headings,     
  tables, fonts, headers/footers, comments, and share URLs—is
  via Google Apps Script (committed to                       
  google_apps_script_project_horizon_carbon4.gs in f53b4141):
                                                             
  #### 30-Second Execution Steps                             
                                                             
  1. Open https://script.google.com in Chrome and click New  
  project.                                                   
  2. Replace Code.gs with the script below (or copy from     
  google_apps_script_project_horizon_carbon4.gs), click Save,
  and click Run (updateProjectHorizonToCarbon4):             
                                                             
    const TARGET_FOLDER_NAME = 'Project Horizon';            
    const DRY_RUN = false; // Set to true first if you want a
    read-only preview                                        
                                                             
    function updateProjectHorizonToCarbon4() {               
      const folders =                                        
      DriveApp.getFoldersByName(TARGET_FOLDER_NAME);         
      if (!folders.hasNext()) {                              
        Logger.log('[ERROR] No Google Drive folder found     
        named "' + TARGET_FOLDER_NAME + '".');               
        return;                                              
      }                                                      
      let totalDocsScanned = 0, totalDocsUpdated = 0;        
      while (folders.hasNext()) {                            
        const rootFolder = folders.next();                   
        Logger.log('[FOLDER] Scanning "' +                   
        rootFolder.getName() + '" (ID: ' + rootFolder.getId()
        + ')');                                              
        const stats = processFolderRecursive_(rootFolder);   
        totalDocsScanned += stats.scanned;                   
        totalDocsUpdated += stats.updated;                   
      }                                                      
      Logger.log('[COMPLETE] Docs Scanned: ' +               
      totalDocsScanned + ' | Docs Updated: ' +               
      totalDocsUpdated);                                     
    }                                                        
                                                             
    function processFolderRecursive_(folder) {               
      let scanned = 0, updated = 0;                          
      const files =                                          
      folder.getFilesByType(MimeType.GOOGLE_DOCS);           
      while (files.hasNext()) {                              
        scanned++;                                           
        if (sweepGoogleDoc_(files.next())) updated++;        
      }                                                      
      const subFolders = folder.getFolders();                
      while (subFolders.hasNext()) {                         
        const s = processFolderRecursive_(subFolders.next());
        scanned += s.scanned;                                
        updated += s.updated;                                
      }                                                      
      return { scanned, updated };                           
    }                                                        
                                                             
    function sweepGoogleDoc_(file) {                         
      const originalName = file.getName();                   
      const doc = DocumentApp.openById(file.getId());        
      const sections = [];                                   
      if (doc.getBody()) sections.push({ label: 'Body', el:  
      doc.getBody() });                                      
      if (doc.getHeader()) sections.push({ label: 'Header',  
      el: doc.getHeader() });                                
      if (doc.getFooter()) sections.push({ label: 'Footer',  
      el: doc.getFooter() });                                
      doc.getFootnotes().forEach((fn, i) => {                
        if (fn.getFootnoteContents()) sections.push({ label: 
        'Footnote ' + (i + 1), el: fn.getFootnoteContents()  
        });                                                  
      });                                                    
                                                             
      const rules = [                                        
        { pattern: '(?i)Gemi[nm]i\\s+Argon\\s+4',            
        replacement: 'Gemini Carbon 4' },                    
        { pattern: '(?i)\\bArgon-4\\b', replacement:         
        'Carbon-4' },                                        
        { pattern: '(?i)\\bArgon\\s+4\\b', replacement:      
        'Carbon 4' }                                         
      ];                                                     
                                                             
      const hitSections = [];                                
      sections.forEach(sec => {                              
        if                                                   
        (/Gemi[nm]i\s+Argon\s+4|\bArgon[-\s]+4\b/i.test(sec.e
        l.getText())) {                                      
          hitSections.push(sec.label);                       
          if (!DRY_RUN) rules.forEach(r =>                   
          sec.el.replaceText(r.pattern, r.replacement));     
        }                                                    
      });                                                    
                                                             
      const newName = originalName                           
        .replace(/Gemi[nm]i\s+Argon\s+4/gi, 'Gemini Carbon   
        4')                                                  
        .replace(/\bArgon-4\b/gi, 'Carbon-4')                
        .replace(/\bArgon\s+4\b/gi, 'Carbon 4');             
      const titleChanged = newName !== originalName;         
      if (titleChanged && !DRY_RUN) file.setName(newName);   
                                                             
      if (hitSections.length > 0 || titleChanged) {          
        if (!DRY_RUN) doc.saveAndClose();                    
        Logger.log('[' + (DRY_RUN ? 'WOULD UPDATE' :         
        'UPDATED') + '] "' + originalName + '" | Sections: ' 
        + hitSections.join(', '));                           
        return true;                                         
      }                                                      
      Logger.log('[CLEAN] "' + originalName + '"');          
      return false;                                          
    }

  ## Turning Option A Into a Competitive Differentiator      
  ("Zero Accreditation Collision")                           
                                                             
  ### The Strategic Hook: Solving the HLC vs. Dual-Enrollment
  Dilemma                                                    
                                                             
  Most colleges, state workforce boards, and EdTech vendors  
  are trapped in a catch-22 when scaling Dual-Enrollment,    
  Perkins V CTE, WIOA, or NSF TechAccess: AI-Ready America   
  (NSF 26-508) cohorts:                                      
                                                             
  • Put High School Standards (CCSS / WA.ELA) on a College   
  Syllabus: Regional accreditors (HLC / NWCCU) and university
  transfer boards (AZTransfer) question whether the course is
  secondary-leveled rather than collegiate.                  
  • Leave High School Standards Out Completely: K–12 Dual-   
  Enrollment / Running Start districts cannot map Grade 11–12
  graduation credit, and OER Commons / Google Dataset Search 
  (LRMI educationalAlignment) harvesters miss the course in  
  K–16 search.                                               
                                                             
  Your S-A-R v2.2 Differentiator: Webcognita's Dual-Namespace
  (EXW → KIN/HLTH) & 4-Tier Standards Compiler               
  (educational_alignment_registry.json +                     
  build_oer_syndication_export.py) solves both simultaneously
  from one JSON registry:                                    
                                                             
  1. Collegiate Syllabus Plane: Protects 100% HLC /          
  university-transfer credit rigor (Procedure 601.3 / 615.3) 
  with zero K–12 dilution.                                   
  2. K–16 & Workforce Syndication Plane: Automatically       
  compiles machine-readable Tier 1 (Federal Clinical SSoT),  
  Tier 2 (U.S. DOL TEN No. 07-25 & NSF AI-Ready), Tier 3 (HLC
  ILOs), and Tier 4 (CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.W.11-12.6, RST.11-12.7,
  WA.ELA.11-12.W.6 — or any of the 50 states' CTE/Dual-      
  Enrollment codes in <5 minutes) into Module 00 reference   
  crosswalks, SHA-256 .zip OER packages, and Schema.         
  org/Dataset JSON-LD.

  alanpruitt.com deploys via GitHub Actions (deploy.yml), and
  the prior workflow runs failed before Hugo ever built      
  because npx playwright install chromium --with-deps called 
  apt-get against azure.archive.ubuntu.com (which was failing
  DNS resolution on GitHub's Ubuntu runner while trying to   
  fetch optional X11 bitmap fonts). Because all Chromium     
  shared libraries are already pre-installed on ubuntu-latest,
  switching deploy.yml:37-38 to npx playwright install       
  chromium bypasses apt-get completely.

    What if I didn't trace the lineage?                      
                                                             
    Today my Curriculum-as-Code (CaC) Origin Whitepaper went

    Yet flat Markdown and LaTeX pipelines still leave        
    clinical truth, LMS accessibility, and FERPA privacy

  ### 1. Why 1x/Week Wednesday Is the Optimal Frequency (Not 
  2x/Week)                                                   
                                                             
  • LinkedIn Carousel Dwell-Time Tail (72–96 Hours):         
  Document-First PDF carousel posts (~2,500 chars) continue  
  compounding impressions from Wednesday morning through     
  Saturday. Posting twice a week cannibalizes your own       
  carousel reach and lowers Substack open rates.             
  • Reviewer Psychology: For Contracting Officers (COs/CORs) 
  and Grant PIs, a steady weekly Wednesday dispatch signals  
  disciplined operational tempo (Slow is Smooth, Smooth is   
  Fast) rather than a rushed marketing blitz.

  capabilities-statement.html 100%

> What is ORCID

▸ Thought for 14s, 115 tokens

  ORCID stands for Open Researcher and Contributor ID        
  (https://orcid.org/). It is a free, permanent 16-digit     
  alphanumeric digital identifier (formatted like            
  https://orcid.org/0009-000X-XXXX-XXXX) operated by a global
  nonprofit registry for faculty, researchers, open-source   
  architects, and federal grant contributors.                
                                                             
  In plain English: ORCID is to an individual researcher or  
  Principal Investigator what a SAM.gov UEI (EZ34U9KNJA17) is
  to Webcognita LLC—a permanent, globally unique serial      
  number that guarantees machines never confuse your work    
  with someone else who shares your name.                    
                                                             
  ### Why ORCID Matters Specifically for Alan Pruitt &       
  Webcognita LLC                                             
                                                             
  1. Permanent Homonym Disambiguation in Google's Knowledge  
  Graph:                                                     
      • Because other professionals share the name "Alan     
      Pruitt" (such as Alan B. Pruitt, CPA), search engines  
      and AI answer engines rely on structured identity      
      graphs to separate individuals.                        
      • Linking an orcid.org ID inside Schema.org/Person     
      (sameAs on index.html and index.html) gives Google,    
      Perplexity, and Google Scholar a cryptographic tie     
      between Alan Lee Pruitt, Webcognita LLC, Arizona       
      Western College, The University of Arizona (DCC), and  
      your Curriculum-as-Code (S-A-R v2.2) publications.     
  2. Federal Grant & Subaward Standard (NSF, NIH, U.S. DOL,  
  U.S. ED, SciENcv):                                         
      • Federal research and workforce agencies (NSF under   
      PAPPG / NSF 26-508 AI-Ready America, NIH, USDA, and    
      SciENcv) use ORCID as the official persistent          
      identifier for Key Personnel, Co-PIs, and subaward     
      technical leads. Having an active ORCID on             
      principal-qualifications.html lets a university PI     
      import your credentials into SciENcv in seconds.       
  3. High-Authority Page-1 SERP Slot (DR 94):                
      • Public orcid.org profiles carry massive domain trust 
      (DR 94), are 100% free (registration takes ~2 minutes  
      with your @arizona.edu or @azwestern.edu institutional 
      email for instant verified-affiliation badges), and    
      allow outbound verified links back to                  
      https://alanpruitt.com/ and https://www.webcognita.com/.
  4. Automatic DOI & Dataset Attribution (Zenodo / OER       
  Commons / Google Scholar):                                 
      • Once registered, your Origin White Paper (Tech.      
      Report S-A-R-v2.2-ORIGIN), your 92-Entry Master        
      Research Log dataset, and your 5 $0 ZTC OER course     
      packages (KIN-101 through KIN-265) can all attach to   
      your single ORCID record.                              
                                                             
                                                             
  If you register a free ORCID at https://orcid.org/register 
  (ideally linking your @arizona.edu and/or @azwestern.edu   
  email) and paste the 16-digit URL here, I can wire it into 
  your Schema.org/Person sameAs graphs,                      
  principal-qualifications.html, capabilities-statement.html,
  and both llms.txt manifests immediately.

  (Aligned to NSF SciENcv)                                   
                                                             
  First, one structural distinction: ORCID (orcid.org) is a  
  bibliographic registry, not a PDF file host — it stores    
  citations, URLs, and DOIs rather than raw PDF uploads.

  products (5 Most Closely Related + 5 Other Significant     
  Products). Flooding ORCID with all 40 essays would dilute  
  your record into a blog feed; curating 9–10 formal papers, 
  manuals, and datasets makes it read like a Principal

▸ Thought for 16s, 943 tokens

  Neither SAM.gov nor OER Commons has a dedicated native     
  database field for an ORCID iD, because each sits on a     
  different layer of the federal and open-education          
  stack—though both connect to it indirectly:                
                                                             
  ### 1. SAM.gov (Entity Layer vs. Federal NSPM-33 Individual
  Layer)                                                     
                                                             
  • Inside SAM.gov Core Data: No. SAM.gov tracks legal       
  entities (Webcognita LLC) via UEI (EZ34U9KNJA17) and CAGE  
  (4ZCN6). Its Entity Registration and Points of Contact     
  forms do not have an ORCID input field.                    
  • Where Federal Agencies Do Pair SAM.gov + ORCID: Under    
  National Security Presidential Memorandum-33 (NSPM-33),    
  federal grant and R&D systems (NSF Research.gov, SciENcv,  
  Grants.gov, NIH, and DOE) require both Identifiers side by 
  side:                                                      
      • Organization DPI: SAM.gov UEI (EZ34U9KNJA17)         
      • Principal / Key Personnel DPI: ORCID iD (0009-0002-  
      5038-7111) — which is why having both printed on your  
      Webcognita_LLC_Principal_Qualifications_CV.pdf and     
      Webcognita_LLC_Capabilities_Statement.pdf closes the   
      federal vetting loop.

▸ Thought for 14s, 866 tokens

  Short answer: Yes—on webcognita.com, as long as we avoid   
  the classic GitHub Pages security trap.                    
                                                             
  ### First: The OPSEC Guardrail                             
                                                             
  Both webcognita.com and alanpruitt.com are static sites    
  served by GitHub Pages from public GitHub repositories     
  (with DNS on Namecheap).                                   
                                                             
  • GitHub Pages has no server-side password gate and no     
  browser file-upload backend.                               
  • If we put a plain HTML password prompt in front of       
  unencrypted PDFs, anyone could bypass the password simply  
  by viewing github.com/alanpruitt/webcognita. Never commit  
  unencrypted signed W-9s, banking/ACH forms, DD-214 / VA    
  SDVOSB letters, or tax transcripts to a public repo.
